target.statement: S2J-Qwen2.5-7B achieves an average solve-to-judge gap P(j=0|s=1) of 21.1% (Delta = -16.2) on the PPE objective subsets MMLU-Pro, MATH and GPQA.
target.table_ref: Table 2, S2J-Qwen2.5-7B (Ours) row, Average and Delta columns
target.dataset: PPE objective subsets: MMLU-Pro, MATH, GPQA

compute.basis: The target requires training a 7B generative reward model with DAPO/GRPO on 300 RL steps, batch size 128 and 16 responses per prompt with max response length 8192, which the paper runs on 8 NVIDIA H800 GPUs and is practically infeasible on an 8-core CPU/16GB laptop; the paper also releases no code or trained checkpoint.

blockers: No code or model checkpoint link in the paper (PDF Links list is empty)
Training S2J-Qwen2.5-7B requires 8 NVIDIA H800 GPUs in the paper setup
DAPO/GRPO RL on Qwen2.5-7B with 16 rollouts, 8192 max response length and 300 steps is infeasible on a normal laptop
Evaluation of a 7B GRM on four reward-model benchmarks is GPU-class inference in practice
Training data synthesis uses Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct and multiple public preference datasets
title: S2J: Bridging the Gap Between Solving and Judging Ability in Generative Reward Models
